description: This chart displays the distribution of CoT (Chain-of-Thought) reasoning outcomes across three difficulty levels—easy, medium, and hard—for a knowledge-based puzzle task, likely knowledge crosswords, as suggested by the paper title. Each difficulty level is represented by a separate pie chart, and all three share the same legend indicating four categories: N+K+ (dark teal), N−K+ (light brown/tan), N−K− (darker brown), and N+K− (reddish-brown). The easy difficulty chart is divided into four segments: N+K+ at 40.6% (dark teal), N−K+ at 45.9% (light brown/tan), N−K− at 10.1% (darker brown), and N+K− at 3.3% (reddish-brown). The medium difficulty chart also has four segments: N+K+ at 44.6% (dark teal), N−K+ at 44.3% (light brown/tan), N−K− at 7.2% (darker brown), and N+K− at 3.9% (reddish-brown). The hard difficulty chart is divided into four segments: N+K+ at 36.2% (dark teal), N−K+ at 36.8% (light brown/tan), N−K− at 7.0% (darker brown), and N+K− at 20.1% (reddish-brown). All pie charts include percentage labels within their respective slices, and the legend is positioned to the right of the hard chart. The slices appear to be ordered in descending size within each chart, with the largest segment appearing first.
